vern.zht: 當初，杜恕從[[趙|/zh-hant/maps/map-overall?admin=159]]郡回來，[[陳留|/zh-hant/maps/map-overall?admin=39]]人阮武也從[[清河|/zh-hant/maps/map-overall?lat=36.91514604&lng=115.75902922&name=Qinghe]][[太守|/zh-hant/translations/officials/regional#commanderies-039]]任上被徵召，兩人都到了[[廷尉|/zh-hant/translations/officials/ministers#-nine-ministers-ii-221]]那裏接受審問。阮武對杜恕說：“我看，您的才性可以遵循公道，但守持得不夠嚴格；器能可以身居高位，但謀求起來卻不順遂；才學可以記述古今，但志向不夠專一。這就是所謂有那樣的才能卻沒有發揮那樣的作用。如今即將有空閒，可以試着潛心思考，寫成一家之言。”杜恕在[[章武|/zh-hant/maps/map-overall?lat=38.56299818&lng=117.17636367&name=Zhangwu]]時，便撰寫了《體論》八節，又寫了《興性論》一篇，大概是爲自身修養而發的。四年，在流放地去世。
vern.zhs: 当初，杜恕从[[赵|/zh-hans/maps/map-overall?admin=159]]郡回来，[[陈留|/zh-hans/maps/map-overall?admin=39]]人阮武也从[[清河|/zh-hans/maps/map-overall?lat=36.91514604&lng=115.75902922&name=Qinghe]][[太守|/zh-hans/translations/officials/regional#commanderies-039]]任上被征召，两人都到了[[廷尉|/zh-hans/translations/officials/ministers#-nine-ministers-ii-221]]那里接受审问。阮武对杜恕说：“我看，您的才性可以遵循公道，但守持得不够严格；器能可以身居高位，但谋求起来却不顺遂；才学可以记述古今，但志向不够专一。这就是所谓有那样的才能却没有发挥那样的作用。如今即将有空闲，可以试着潜心思考，写成一家之言。”杜恕在[[章武|/zh-hans/maps/map-overall?lat=38.56299818&lng=117.17636367&name=Zhangwu]]时，便撰写了《体论》八节，又写了《兴性论》一篇，大概是为自身修养而发的。四年，在流放地去世。

passages.en: Previously, when Du Shu returned from [[Zhao|/maps/map-overall?admin=159]], Ruan Wu of [[Chenliu|/maps/map-overall?admin=39]] was likewise [[recalled|/translations/officials#glossary-summon]] from his post as [[Grand Administrator|/translations/officials/regional#commanderies-039]] of [[Qinghe|/maps/map-overall?lat=36.91514604&lng=115.75902922&name=Qinghe]]. Both appeared before the [[Commandant of Justice|/translations/officials/ministers#-nine-ministers-ii-221]]. Ruan Wu said to Du Shu, "As I see it, you have the talent and character to follow the Way, yet lack firmness in upholding it; you have the capacity to hold high office, yet your path to advancement is beset with obstacles; and you have the learning to expound past and present, yet lack singleness of purpose. This is what is meant by possessing talent without putting it to use. Now that you have leisure, devote yourself to quiet reflection and set forth a teaching of your own." While at [[Zhangwu|/maps/map-overall?lat=38.56299818&lng=117.17636367&name=Zhangwu]], Du Shu accordingly wrote the Discourse on Fundamentals in eight sections, and another essay entitled Discourse on Arousing the Nature. Both likely sprang from his commitment to self-cultivation. In the fourth year, he died in exile.

annotations.zhs: 《杜氏新书》曰：以为人伦之大纲，莫重于君臣；立身之基本，莫大于言行；安上理民，莫精于政法；胜残去杀，莫善于用兵。夫礼也者，万物之体也，万物皆得其体，无有不善，故谓之体论。

vern.zht: 《杜氏新書》集中：杜恕認爲人倫的大綱，沒有比君臣關係更重要的；安身立命的根本，沒有比言行更重要的。安定君主、治理百姓，沒有比政法更精深的；遏制殘暴、消除殺戮，沒有比用兵更有效的。禮，是萬物的根本準則。萬物都遵循了禮這個根本，就不會有不好的地方，所以把這本書命名爲《體論》。
vern.zhs: 《杜氏新书》集中：杜恕认为人伦的大纲，没有比君臣关系更重要的；安身立命的根本，没有比言行更重要的。安定君主、治理百姓，没有比政法更精深的；遏制残暴、消除杀戮，没有比用兵更有效的。礼，是万物的根本准则。万物都遵循了礼这个根本，就不会有不好的地方，所以把这本书命名为《体论》。

annotations.en: The Du Shi Xinshu / New Book of Du Clan states: Du Shu held that of the cardinal bonds of human society, none was weightier than that between ruler and subject; of the foundations of personal conduct, none was greater than speech and action; for securing the ruler and governing the people, nothing surpassed institutions and laws; and for subduing cruelty and putting an end to killing, nothing was better than the art of war. Ritual gives form to all things, and when all things attain their proper form, all are brought to goodness. Hence he called the work the Discourse on Form.

passages.en: In the second year of Ganlu, Yue Xiang of [[Hedong|/maps/map-overall?admin=57]], then over ninety, submitted a memorial recounting Du Ji's lasting achievements. The court was moved and decreed that Du Shu's son Du Yu be enfeoffed as [[Neighbourhood Marquis|/translations/officials#glossary-capital-neighbourhood-neighbourhood-marquis]] of Fengle, with a fief of one hundred households. Du Shu's memorials, proposals, arguments, and rebuttals are all worthy of attention. Those bearing most directly on the great affairs of his age are recorded here.

《魏略》曰：樂詳字文載。少好學，建安初，詳聞[[公車司馬令|/zh-hant/translations/officials/ministers#-nine-ministers-i-198]][[南|/zh-hant/maps/map-overall?admin=80]]郡謝該善左氏傳，乃從[[南陽|/zh-hant/maps/map-overall?admin=85]]步詣該，問疑難諸要，今左氏樂氏問七十二事，詳所撰也。所問旣了而歸鄉里，時杜畿為[[太守|/zh-hant/translations/officials/regional#commanderies-039]]，亦甚好學，[[署|/zh-hant/translations/officials#glossary-deputise]]詳[[文學祭酒|/zh-hant/translations/officials/regional#commanderies-054]]，使教後進，於是[[河東|/zh-hant/maps/map-overall?admin=57]]學業大興。

《魏略》記載：樂詳，字文載，年少時就喜愛學習。建安初年，樂詳聽說[[公車司馬令|/zh-hant/translations/officials/ministers#-nine-ministers-i-198]]、[[南|/zh-hant/maps/map-overall?admin=80]]郡人謝該擅長講解《左氏傳》，就從[[南陽|/zh-hant/maps/map-overall?admin=85]]步行前往拜訪他，詢問諸多疑難要點。如今《左氏樂氏問》中的七十二件事，是樂詳所撰寫的。當所問的問題都已經弄清楚後，他就回到了家鄉。當時杜畿擔任[[太守|/zh-hant/translations/officials/regional#commanderies-039]]，也非常好學，任命樂詳爲[[文學祭酒|/zh-hant/translations/officials/regional#commanderies-054]]，讓他教導後輩學生。於是[[河東|/zh-hant/maps/map-overall?admin=57]]的學術事業十分興盛起來。

到了黃初年間，朝廷徵召樂詳並任命他爲博士。當時太學剛剛設立，有十多位博士，學問大多淺陋狹窄，又不熟悉教學，幾乎不親自授課，只是充數罷了。只有樂詳同時教授五經。有的問題很難理解，向他詢問也還是不明白，樂詳也沒有生氣的神色，用手杖在地上比劃，旁徵博引、類比舉例，甚至到了廢寢忘食的地步，因此他獨遠近聞名。樂詳的學問精深全面，又擅長推算天文曆法，朝廷另外下詔讓他和太史一起制定曆法。太和年間，他轉任[[騎都尉|/zh-hant/translations/officials/ministers#-nine-ministers-i-178]]。詳學識優秀但能力不足，因此歷經三代，最終沒有出任地方長官。到正始年間，因爲年老退休回家。他本鄉的宗族都歸附他，門徒有數千人。

The Weilüe / Brief History of Wei states: Yue Xiang, courtesy name Wenzai, was fond of learning from an early age. At the beginning of the Jian'an era, he heard that Xie Gai of [[Nan|/maps/map-overall?admin=80]] Commandery, [[Director of Official Carriages at Sima Gate|/translations/officials/ministers#-nine-ministers-i-198]], was well versed in the Zuo Tradition. He therefore travelled on foot from [[Nanyang|/maps/map-overall?admin=85]] to visit him and seek answers to doubts and difficulties. The extant Master Yue's Seventy-Two Questions on the Zuo Tradition was written by Xiang. Once his questions had been resolved, he returned home. At the time, Du Ji was [[Grand Administrator|/translations/officials/regional#commanderies-039]] of [[Hedong|/maps/map-overall?admin=57]]. He too was deeply devoted to learning and [[appointed|/translations/officials#glossary-deputise]] Yue Xiang [[Literary Section Libationer|/translations/officials/regional#commanderies-054]], entrusting him with the instruction of younger scholars. Thereafter, learning flourished greatly in Hedong. 

During the Huangchu era, Yue Xiang was [[summoned|/translations/officials#glossary-summon]] and [[appointed|/translations/officials#glossary-formally-appoint]] an Erudite. The Imperial Academy had only recently been established, with only ten or so Erudites. Most were narrow in their learning and lacked mastery of their subjects. They seldom taught in person and merely filled their posts. Yue Xiang alone taught all five classics. When some pupils proved difficult to teach and still failed to understand after repeated questioning, Yue Xiang showed no anger. Drawing diagrams on the ground with his staff, he used analogies and comparable examples to explain the matter, often forgetting sleep and food. Thus he alone won renown far and wide. Yue Xiang possessed both profound and comprehensive learning and was also skilled in calendrical calculation. By a separate edict, he was ordered to work with the Grand Astrologer in establishing the standard calendar. During the Taihe era, he was [[transferred|/translations/officials#glossary-transfer]] to [[Commandant of Cavalry|/translations/officials/ministers#-nine-ministers-i-178]]. Though eminent in scholarship, Xiang lacked administrative abilities. Consequently, through three reigns, he was never sent out to serve as governor or Grand Administrator. During the Zhengshi era, Yue Xiang retired on account of old age and returned home. He was highly esteemed by the clans of his native commandery, and his disciples numbered several thousand.

vern.zht: 《杜氏新書》記載：杜恕的弟弟杜理，字務仲，年少時就機敏明察、能抓住關鍵要點，杜畿認爲他很奇特，所以給他取名爲理。他二十一歲就去世了。另一個弟弟杜寬，字務叔，淡泊寧靜，聰明而喜好古代文化事物。因爲出身於名臣之家，從小在京城長大，卻志向堅定，學識淵博，不參與世俗的事務，只想要探究幽深隱微的道理，因此他名聲顯著，當權的人大多和他交往。他被推舉爲[[孝廉|/zh-hant/translations/officials#glossary-filial-and-incorrupt]]，被任命爲郎中，四十二歲時去世。他對於經傳的義理，有很多自己的論述和辯駁，但都只是初稿沒有完成，只有刪集的《禮記》和《春秋左氏傳解》，如今流傳於世。

annotations.en: The Du Shi Xinshu / New Book of Du Clan states: Du Shu's younger brother Du Li, courtesy name Wuzhong, was keenly perceptive from an early age and had a fine grasp of essentials. Du Ji thought him remarkable and therefore named him Li. He died aged twenty-one. Du Shu's younger brother Kuan, courtesy name Wushu, was pure and detached, profound and tranquil, quick-witted and fond of antiquity. Born into the family of an eminent minister, he grew up in the capital. Yet he devoted himself to broad learning and withdrew entirely from worldly affairs, intent on probing the abstruse and uncovering the hidden. He thereby gained renown, and many men in positions of influence befriended him. He was nominated as a [[Filial and Incorrupt|/translations/officials#glossary-filial-and-incorrupt]] and appointed Gentleman of the Household. He died aged forty-two. Du Kuan produced many critical discussions of the meanings of the Classics and their commentaries, but all remained unfinished drafts. Only his edited compilation of the Record of Rites and his explanations of Zuo's Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals survive today.

杜預字元凱，是司馬宣王的女婿。王隱的《晉書》稱杜預智謀淵博，明白治亂之道，他常說：“道德方面，不是自己所能達到的，建立功業、著書立說，或許自己還能做到。”杜預廣泛閱覽各種典籍，認爲《公羊傳》《穀梁傳》是詭辯的言論，也不符合先代儒家的學說。前人對《左傳》的註釋沒有探究到左丘明的本意，還隨意用《公羊傳》《穀梁傳》的內容混淆《左傳》，於是杜預梳理《左傳》中的精深微妙的言辭，撰寫了《春秋左氏經傳集解》，又參考了其他各家學說，把它稱爲《釋例》。又創作了《盟會圖》《春秋長曆》，完備地形成了自成一家的學說，到年老時才完成。[[尚書郎|/zh-hant/translations/officials/departments#state-affairs-037]]摯虞非常看重他的這些著作，說：“左丘明本來是爲《春秋》作傳，而《左傳》於是獨自流傳。《釋例》本來是爲《左傳》而作，但它所闡發的道理，又豈止是《左傳》，所以它也能獨立流傳。”

杜預在晉朝立下了很大的功勳和名聲，官至[[征南大將軍|/zh-hant/translations/officials/military#conquering--garrisoning-065]]，[[開府|/zh-hant/translations/officials#glossary-open-office]]，被封爲[[當陽|/zh-hant/maps/map-overall?lat=30.83899565&lng=112.01347539&name=Dangyang]]侯，食邑八千戶。他的兒子杜嘏，擔任[[尚書左丞|/zh-hant/translations/officials/departments#state-affairs-034]]。

Du Yu, courtesy name Yuankai, was the son-in-law of Sima Yi. Wang Yin's Book of Jin records that Du Yu possessed profound intelligence and strategic insight, and clearly understood the principles of good government. Du Yu often said, "To establish virtue lies beyond the reach of men like me; but to establish merit and leave words behind are things that ordinary men may accomplish." After surveying the classical canon, he deemed the Gongyang and Guliang traditions as merely specious arguments. He also criticised earlier scholars for failing to grasp Zuo Qiuming's intent and arbitrarily confusing his work with those two traditions. Weaving together the text's subtle meanings, he composed the Collected Explanations of the Classic and Commentary of Master Zuo on the Spring and Autumn Annals. He also consulted the works of many scholars to produce the Explication of Precedents, as well as the Charts of Covenants and Assemblies and the Long Chronology of the Spring and Autumn Annals. Together these formed a complete school of scholarship, but he did not finish them until old age. Zhi Yu, an [[Imperial Secretariat Court Gentleman|/translations/officials/departments#state-affairs-037]], esteemed his works highly, saying: "Zuo Qiuming originally wrote his commentary for the Spring and Autumn Annals, yet the Zuo Commentary came to circulate independently. The Explication of Precedents was originally written for that commentary, but what it illuminates is by no means confined to the Zuo Commentary. It too should therefore circulate independently." 

Du Yu rendered distinguished service to the house of Jin. He rose to become [[Grand General Who Conquers the South|/translations/officials/military#conquering--garrisoning-065]], received the privilege to [[Open Office|/translations/officials#glossary-open-office]], and was enfeoffed as Marquis of [[Dangyang|/maps/map-overall?lat=30.83899565&lng=112.01347539&name=Dangyang]], with a fief of eight thousand households. His son Du Xi, courtesy name Shigu, served as [[Imperial Secretariat Left Assistant|/translations/officials/departments#state-affairs-034]].

annotations.en: The Jin Zhugong Zan / Appraisal of Officials of Jin states: "Du Gu possessed both ability and breadth of mind." Du Yu's elder cousin Du Wu, courtesy name Shijiang, was likewise talented and highly regarded. He served as [[Gentleman within the Yellow Gates|/translations/officials/departments#chancellery-003]], but was unjustly executed by Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao. Du Gu's son Du Yi, courtesy name Hongzhi, won a fine reputation in his youth. He served as [[Assistant to the Grand Administrator|/translations/officials/regional#commanderies-040]] of [[Danyang|/maps/map-overall?admin=60]], but died young. Ruan Wu was also a man of unfettered spirit and great talent. According to the Genealogy of the Ruan Clan, his father Ruan Chen, courtesy name Shixin, declined every [[summons|/translations/officials#glossary-summon]] and [[recruitment|/translations/officials#glossary-recruit]]. He compiled the Illustrations of the Three Rites, which circulated throughout the realm.

annotations.en: The Du Shi Xinshu / New Book of Du Clan states: Ruan Wu, courtesy name Wenye, was broad-minded and widely learned, and a man of profound refinement. He rose no higher than [[Grand Administrator|/translations/officials/regional#commanderies-039]] of [[Qinghe|/maps/map-overall?lat=36.91514604&lng=115.75902922&name=Qinghe]]. His younger brother Ruan Bing, courtesy name Shuwen, served as [[Intendant of Henan|/translations/officials/regional#commanderies-032]]. Ruan Bing devoted himself to medicine and compiled a volume of prescriptions. Ruan Bing's son Ruan Tan, courtesy name Hongshu, served under the Jin as [[Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince|/translations/officials/household#eastern-palace-010]] and [[General Who Subdues the East|/translations/officials/military#pacifying--subduing-095]]. Ruan Tan's younger brother Ruan Ke had the courtesy name Shidu.

annotations.en: The Records of Yan province (Xun Chuo) states: Ruan Tan had been adopted to continue the line of their paternal uncle. When their uncle died, he should have inherited the title. Their father, however, favoured Ruan Ke and claimed that Ruan Tan had named him as his heir, so Ruan Ke succeeded to the fief. Ruan Tan was too young to object at the time, but deeply regretted it when he came of age. Thereafter, he wore a plain cloth cap and, even after entering official service, never removed it. Sincere, steadfast, serene, and refined by nature, Ruan Tan observed the rites without fail. He devoted himself to the canonical texts and was widely learned and well informed. He was selected as [[Scholar|/translations/officials/regional#states-087]] to the Prince of [[Puyang|/maps/map-overall?lat=35.61104535&lng=114.9728879&name=Puyang]], then [[promoted|/translations/officials#glossary-reassign]] to [[Chief Clerk|/translations/officials/military#central-army-003]] to the [[Commander of the Central Army|/translations/officials/military#central-army-001]]. He died in office. Wang Yan, then [[Commander of the Central Army|/translations/officials/military#central-army-001]], wept for him in profound grief.
